# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-knx/server"
```

Package server is a KNXnet/IP server: it answers discovery (search, extended search) and description requests, accepts tunnelling connections from KNXnet/IP clients, and optionally routes over IP multicast. Behind it is a virtual KNX network instead of a physical line: telegrams of one client are confirmed to it and delivered to the other clients, to the virtual devices (package device) and, with routing, to the multicast group.

What it implements:

  - core services: search, extended search, description, connect, connection state, disconnect;
  - tunnelling over UDP and over TCP ([WithTCP](#func-withtcp), on by default): the link layer (including the extended CRI that requests an address and route back endpoints) and the busmonitor layer ([WithConcurrentBusmonitor](#func-withconcurrentbusmonitor) lets it coexist with tunnels); over TCP also the tunnelling feature services (tunnelling v2);
  - device management connections (local property read and write of the server's interface objects) and remote device management of the server's own device through a tunnel (property read, write and description), with [WithToolKey](#func-withtoolkey) secured by KNX Data Secure tool access;
  - routing indications ([WithRouting](#func-withrouting)), queued and paced by routing flow control: at most [WithRoutingRate](#func-withroutingrate) per second, and a pause after a ROUTING\_BUSY from another router;
  - KNX IP Secure: secure tunnelling sessions over TCP and UDP ([WithSecure](#func-withsecure), ended after [WithSecureSessionTimeout](#func-withsecuresessiontimeout) idle) and secure routing ([WithSecureRouting](#func-withsecurerouting)).

Raw tunnelling and other connection types are refused with the standard status codes. It is not an emulation of a KNX TP line or of a physical device's management.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// DefaultConnectionAliveTime is CONNECTION_ALIVE_TIME: a tunnelling
	// connection without a CONNECTIONSTATE_REQUEST for this long is
	// closed.
	DefaultConnectionAliveTime = 120 * time.Second
	// DefaultSecureSessionTimeout is SESSION_TIMEOUT: a KNX IP Secure
	// session without a frame for this long is ended.
	DefaultSecureSessionTimeout = 60 * time.Second
	// DefaultSecureAuthTimeout bounds the time from SESSION_REQUEST to a
	// successful SESSION_AUTHENTICATE: a KNX IP Secure session (or a TCP
	// connection of a secure server) that has not authenticated by then
	// is ended.
	DefaultSecureAuthTimeout = 10 * time.Second
	// DefaultQueueSize bounds the telegrams queued for each tunnelling
	// connection.
	DefaultQueueSize = 128
	// DefaultRoutingRate bounds the ROUTING_INDICATIONs the server sends
	// per second. The standard asks routers not to flood the IP network;
	// 50 telegrams per second is the rate of a TP1 line.
	DefaultRoutingRate = 50
)
```

Defaults.

```go
const (
	// DeviceDescriptor is the device descriptor type 0 the server reports:
	// 0x091A, a KNXnet/IP router.
	DeviceDescriptor = 0x091A
	// MaxAPDU is the longest APDU the server passes (extended frames).
	MaxAPDU = 254
)
```

Server constants reported by device management and the tunnelling interface features.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*options) error
```

Option configures a [Server](#type-server).

#### func WithConcurrentBusmonitor

```go
func WithConcurrentBusmonitor(on bool) Option
```

WithConcurrentBusmonitor lets busmonitor connections coexist with link layer tunnelling connections. By default they exclude each other, as on a KNX interface: while a busmonitor connection is open, tunnelling connections are refused (E\_NO\_MORE\_CONNECTIONS), and the other way round. Several busmonitor connections are always allowed. A simulator that monitors the telegrams of its own clients needs this option.


#### func WithQueueSize

```go
func WithQueueSize(n int) Option
```

WithQueueSize bounds the telegrams queued for each tunnelling connection and, with routing, the routing indications waiting to be sent (default 128); when a queue is full, telegrams are dropped.

#### func WithRequestTimeout

```go
func WithRequestTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithRequestTimeout sets the wait for a client's TUNNELLING\_ACK (default 1 s).

#### func WithRouting

```go
func WithRouting(on bool) Option
```

WithRouting enables KNXnet/IP routing: telegrams of tunnelling clients and devices are sent as ROUTING\_INDICATIONs to the multicast group, and indications from other routers are delivered to the clients and devices.

#### func WithRoutingRate

```go
func WithRoutingRate(n int) Option
```

WithRoutingRate bounds the routing indications sent per second (default 50; 0 disables the limit): consecutive indications are at least 1/n apart. Indications wait in a queue of WithQueueSize telegrams for their turn and for the pause of a ROUTING\_BUSY; when the queue is full they are dropped and counted (OnDropped "routing\_rate").

#### func WithSecure

```go
func WithSecure(device secure.Key, users map[uint8]SecureUser) Option
```

WithSecure makes the server a KNX IP Secure interface: tunnelling and device management connections need a secure session over TCP (KNXnet/IP Secure, SESSION\_REQUEST...) authenticated as one of the users (IDs 1..127); plain connection requests are refused with E\_CONNECTION\_TYPE. device is the device authentication code (secure.DeviceAuthenticationCode). Device management connections are for user 1, the management user. Search and description stay plain. WithTCP must stay on.

A session must authenticate within [WithSecureAuthTimeout](#func-withsecureauthtimeout); until then its frames do not keep it open, and when the sessions (or TCP connections) are all taken, a new one replaces the oldest that has not authenticated. A tunnel carries only telegrams with its own individual address as source (or 0, which the server replaces).

WithSecure alone does not protect the remote management of the server's own device (property read and write to its individual address through a tunnel): that stays plain for every tunnelling user unless [WithToolKey](#func-withtoolkey) is set.

#### func WithSecureAuthTimeout

```go
func WithSecureAuthTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithSecureAuthTimeout sets how long a KNX IP Secure session of a [WithSecure](#func-withsecure) server, and a TCP connection to it, may stay without an authenticated user (default 10 s): from SESSION\_REQUEST (over TCP from the accept) to a successful SESSION\_AUTHENTICATE. Frames received before that do not extend it.

#### func WithSecureRouting

```go
func WithSecureRouting(key secure.Key, latency time.Duration) Option
```

WithSecureRouting makes the server's routing (WithRouting) KNX IP Secure routing with the backbone key and latency tolerance (0: secure.DefaultLatency): routing frames are sent and accepted only in SECURE\_WRAPPERs, with the synchronised multicast timer.

#### func WithSecureSessionTimeout

```go
func WithSecureSessionTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithSecureSessionTimeout sets how long a KNX IP Secure session ([WithSecure](#func-withsecure), [WithSecureRouting](#func-withsecurerouting) unicast sessions included) may stay without a frame before the server ends it (default 60 s).

#### func WithTCP

```go
func WithTCP(on bool) Option
```

WithTCP sets whether the server also accepts KNXnet/IP over TCP on the same port (default true): core v2 and tunnelling v2 with the tunnelling feature services.

#### func WithToolKey

```go
func WithToolKey(k datasecure.Key) Option
```

WithToolKey secures the remote management of the server's device (its individual address) with KNX Data Secure: the server answers only S-A\_Sync and S-A\_Data with tool access under this tool key, and its interface object list has a security object (security mode on). Without it, remote management is plain.

#### func WithTunnelAddresses

```go
func WithTunnelAddresses(addrs ...knx.IndividualAddress) Option
```

WithTunnelAddresses sets the individual addresses of the tunnelling connections, one per connection: their number is the connection limit (default one, 15.15.250).

```go
)
```

#### func (Server) Send

```go
func (s *Server) Send(f *cemi.LData) error
```

Send puts a telegram on the virtual network as the server: it reaches every tunnelling client, the devices and, with routing, the multicast group. A zero source is replaced by the server's address; the message code becomes L\_Data.ind.

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(ctx context.Context) error
```

Serve starts the server and blocks until ctx is done, then closes it.

#### func (Server) Start

```go
func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error
```

Start opens the sockets and starts serving in the background.

#### func (Server) Subscribe

```go
func (s *Server) Subscribe(f func(Telegram)) (cancel func())
```

Subscribe calls f, synchronously, for every telegram on the virtual network; it must not block. The returned function removes it.

#### func (Server) Transmit

```go
func (s *Server) Transmit(d *device.Device, o *device.GroupObject, v any) error
```

Transmit sets a device's group object to v and, if the object has the C and T flags, sends the A\_GroupValue\_Write as that device.
